   Here is Claude's plan: 
  ╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌╌
   Fix the approve button's last step: the keystroke

   Context

   The feature works end to end except the final keypress. The last attempt proved most of it:

   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │                              Evidence                               │                                          Conclusion                                          │
   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   │ hook.log: 16:50:15 fired … plan=now-you-have-access-abundant-graham │ PreToolUse does fire for ExitPlanMode. The open question from the last plan is answered — no │
   │  … registered                                                       │  need for the Notification fallback.                                                         │
   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   │ The buttons appeared in the browser                                 │ Registration, /api/plans, the awaiting badge and the header controls all work.               │
   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   │ awaiting is now empty — the token was consumed                      │ The click reached /api/approve, passed the same-origin check, and the token validated.       │
   ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
   │ The terminal did not advance                                        │ The failure is isolated to reading the prompt or delivering the keystroke.                   │
   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

   So the remaining bug is in one of two places, and I cannot yet tell which, because /api/approve
   records nothing and an empty awaiting is consistent with both:

   1. Refused (409). parsePrompt did not recognise the real prompt, so nothing was typed. My parser
   was built from an educated guess at the rendering — box-drawing frame, ❯ cursor, Yes…/No…
   option rows — never from a real capture.
   2. Sent (200) but inert. agtermctl session type --stdin reported success, but \x1b[B / \r did
   not register as arrow/Enter in the Claude Code TUI.

   Two things also became clear while diagnosing, both worth fixing:

   - session text accepts --all or --lines, never both — passing both is a hard error. My
   product code only ever passes --lines, so it is unaffected, but two of my manual checks were
   silently reading that error message instead of a terminal buffer.
   - session text returns only the visible screen (~61 lines here); the fullscreen TUI retains no
   scrollback. So the prompt can only be inspected while it is on screen, which is why this needs a
   live capture rather than after-the-fact forensics.

   Step 1 — Capture the real prompt (already running)

   A background poller is watching this session for Ready to code? and will save the first matching
   screen to the scratchpad. Approving this plan produces that prompt, so the capture happens without
   any further setup. That file becomes the fixture the parser is written against.
